title: Swede, bacon and lentil pot with clementine

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Bacon, lentils, stock, kale, swede and clementines are all ordinary home kitchen foods with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at any mainstream UK supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded pan and a wooden spoon, and the crushing and simmering are beginner-level.

works.reason: 200g green lentils, a large swede and 1 litre of stock simmered for 25 minutes give a tender, brothy pot that suits four for lunch, and crushing some swede thickens it sensibly.

honest_times.reason: Peeling and dicing a large swede plus chopping bacon, onion, garlic and kale fits roughly in 20 minutes, and the 35-minute cook matches the 5, 25 and 5 minute steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming swede and lentil pot suits a cold early-January lunch, and swede is the bulk of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English a neighbour would give.

hearty_healthy.reason: Lentils, bacon, swede and kale make a filling, balanced meal a family would happily eat again.
